editorial:
Imagine waking up to find a serial killer is turning the city into a giant puzzle based on the Bible. You get to follow Inspector Niemans and a rookie detective who are totally out of their league until they team up with a religion expert to stop the madness. The whole vibe feels like a high-stakes scavenger hunt where every clue leads to another gruesome crime scene. It is a wild ride that mixes police work with ancient myths, making you feel like you are solving a mystery alongside the characters as they race against a clock to stop the apocalypse.

What really works here is the tension and the strange twists that keep you guessing. The acting is solid, and the action scenes move quickly, though some of the religious talk can get a bit heavy. If you love movies that make you think while giving you a thrill, you will dig this one. You should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or you can rent it on Apple TV if you want a quick movie night. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the killer is actually a high-ranking official who believes he is purifying the world. He tries to complete the cycle of the twelve apostles to trigger a fake apocalypse. In the final showdown, Niemans manages to track him down and stop the last murder just in time. The movie ends with the killer being caught, proving that logic and teamwork can beat even the craziest delusions of grandeur.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves conspiracy theories and detective stories.
